newsitem.title: INDIA: South India state says ban on alcohol to stay.
newsitem.headline: South India state says ban on alcohol to stay.

text.p: India's southern state of Andhra Pradesh will not relax a ban on alcohol which has cost it revenue of around 20 billion rupees ($560 million), a state minister said on Friday.

Presenting the state budget for 1997/98 (April-March), finance minister P. Ashok Gajapathi Raju said there would be no change in the state's policy despite its budget showing a record deficit of 5.62 billion rupees.
Raju's government introduced prohibition in Andhra Pradesh in January 1995, to make good on an election promise.

Political analysts had speculated that Andhra Pradesh might relax the ban to help tide over its difficult financial position, made precarious by the devastation of two cyclones that ripped through the state in June and November last year.
But Raju disappointed the state's tipplers, saying the government would continue to prohibit the drinking of home-brewed and Indian-made foreign liquor.
But the consumption of toddy (country fermented liquor) would be allowed, he added.
Raju said the federal government should compensate state governments imposing prohibition for their revenue losses.
He said the World Bank had indicated its willingness to fund projects for reconstruction worth six billion rupees in cyclone-ravaged areas of the state.
The total loss on account of cyclones and rains during 1996 was 75.77 billion rupees besides the loss of 1,743 human lives.
The minister added that the state government had formulated a programme for providing permanent protection against natural calamities and approached the World Bank for funding assistance.
The Bank was willing to consider a project size of $170 million, with 70 percent coming as World Bank assistance and the rest funded by the state government, Raju said.
